starting-out.player: Hello there. What are you doing here?

options.text: I follow the path of Saradomin.

steps.player: I follow the path of Saradomin. Strength through wisdom.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Ah, a wise choice my friend. But if you truly follow Saradomin, what brings you to these evil lands?

options.text: I come seeking challenges and quests.

steps.player: I come seeking challenges and quests.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: A noble cause indeed. One that I can sympathise with, for I myself am upon a quest.  One that will allow Saradomin to be glorified even in these dark lands.

options.text: Yes.

steps.player: What quest is that then?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Well, below the very ground you stand upon lies an intricate network of tunnels that make up the abandoned Mort Ridge mines. These mines used to be a valuable resource to the inhabitants of Morytania.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: As with many things, this changed when Misthalin was finally able to push the minions of Morytania back, and Saradomin himself blessed the river Salve.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: The mines are also the site where the legendary artefact, the salve amulet, was thought to have been carved from the crystals that grow in the lower levels of the mine.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: These crystals are thought to be formed by the blessed water of the river Salve as it percolates through the rocks to the lower levels of the mine.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: It is not known what happened to the salve amulet, but it is generally believed that by encapsulating within it some of the goodness of Saradomin himself, it afforded the bearer power over evil.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Saradomin has entrusted me alone with the task of regaining access to the mines, whatever the dangers.

steps.player: How can an abandoned mine be dangerous?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Because the mines are said to be haunted. The crystals and the ridge used to be protected by Zamorak's mage, Treus Dayth.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Dayth failed and fell during an incursion by Saradominists, who then made it into the mines and were able to remove a shard of crystal.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Zamorak, furious at his mage, condemned Dayth's soul indefinitely to an existence of turmoil in the mines. Dayth's soul is bound to prevent the crystals from ever being reached again.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Further, Zamorak's then ruler upon the land ordered the slaughter of anyone within the mines and that the mines be sealed.

options.text: Is there any other way into the mines?
How does a lost artefact that was only legendary help?
Why was everyone in the mines slaughtered?
I must be going now.

steps.player: I must be going now, good luck on your quest.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: You should believe not in luck, but in the protection of Saradomin. Farewell.

options.text: No.

steps.player: I hope it goes well.  Goodbye.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Goodbye, and may Saradomin give you strength through wisdom.

options.text: Ok I lied.

steps.player: Ok I lied, I don't support Saradomin. I'm only here for dastardly evil purposes.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Then leave me, I have no time to listen to your poisonous tongue.

options.text: I could ask the same of you.

steps.player: I could ask the same of you.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Saradomin has granted you wisdom. The evil creatures of this land are cunning and you are right to question anyone's purpose here.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I am upon a quest. One that will allow Saradomin to be glorified even in these dark lands.

options.text: I serve only Zamorak.

steps.player: I serve only Zamorak. Strength through chaos.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Then begone.  Normally I would strike you down in an instant, but for now I have no time. I am on a quest of the utmost importance.

options.text: What is this quest of which you speak?

steps.player: What is this quest of which you speak?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: It is no concern of yours, but rest assured it will help in crushing you and those others who serve your vile master.

steps.player: I doubt that.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I would expect nothing less of you, misguided as you already are.

options.text: Fine, I didn't want to talk to you either.

steps.player: Fine, I didn't want to talk to you either.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Fear not fiend, even though I may leave you be, you shall not escape justice at the hands of the righteous.

options.text: My beliefs are in accord with the teachings of Guthix.

steps.player: My beliefs are in accord with the teachings of Guthix. Balance is power.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: A wishy washy set of beliefs. You should follow Saradomin and find a real purpose in your life.

options.text: And what sort of purpose would that be?

steps.player: And what sort of purpose would that be?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: To further the glory of Saradomin of course.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Take myself, I am upon a quest that will allow Saradomin to be glorified even in these dark lands.

options.text: I can make my own choices.

steps.player: I can make my own choices, who are you to dispute them?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I look only to help those who are misguided.

options.text: I have no particular allegiance.

steps.player: I have no particular allegiance.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Then your life is without reason or direction. I would talk to you further on the matter, but for now my attentions must be elsewhere.

options.text: Then I shall leave you to your business.

steps.player: Then I shall leave you to your business.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I shall pray that Saradomin grants you the wisdom to see through your folly.

options.text: Why, what are you doing?

steps.player: Why, what are you doing?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I am upon a quest. One that will allow Saradomin to be glorified even in these dark lands.

starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-again.speaker: Zealot
starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-again.text: Hello again. I'm afraid I'm rather preoccupied. What was it you wanted?

options.text: Can you explain the history of these mines again?

steps.player: Can you explain the history of these mines again?

options.text: Is there any other way into the mines?
options.condition: Before asking if there is any other way in:

steps.player: Is there any other way into the mines?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Indeed I have found hope that this may be so. By making discreet inquiries I have been led to believe that a second entrance may exist into the mines.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Further, I have come into possession of a key that will apparently afford entrance to the lower levels of the mines once inside.

options.text: Where is the second entrance to the mines?

steps.player: Where is the second entrance to the mines?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Of this I am not yet sure. From what I have been able to gather, it was not originally built for humans to enter by. Where it may be, I am still endeavoring to find out.

options.text: How can you be discreet with THAT star emblazoned on your robes?

steps.player: How can you be discreet with THAT star emblazoned on your robes?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Saradomin watches over me, I am not troubled by those who are not meant to notice.

steps.player: Even so, you're not exactly keeping quiet about your allegiance are you?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Saradomin will protect me. Even if I should fall there are many behind me who would stand in my place.

options.text: Is that much consolation?

steps.player: Is that much consolation when you get chopped up into little pieces?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I would rather be cut into little pieces whilst proclaiming the goodness of Saradomin than hiding my faith.

options.text: I can't see anyone behind you.

steps.player: I can't see anyone behind you.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Although you may not realise it, Saradomin works quietly in many people, such is the folly of looking with your eyes and not with your heart.

options.text: And I would be one of them. So, can I borrow that key?

steps.player: And I would be one of them. So, can I borrow that key?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I am afraid my task can be entrusted to nobody else. Saradomin has asked me alone to do this. I cannot take the slightest risk of losing this key. The stakes are too high.

options.text: Please? I'll be very careful with it.
I didn't want that key anyway.
You're right, I was wrong to doubt Saradomin.

steps.player: You're right, I was wrong to doubt Saradomin.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Let not your faith in Saradomin falter, for all else is insignificant.

options.text: You're nuts, goodbye.

steps.player: You're nuts, goodbye.

options.text: Can I borrow your key?

steps.player: Can I borrow your key?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I am afraid my task can be entrusted to nobody else. Saradomin has asked me alone to do this. I cannot take the slightest risk of losing this key. The stakes are too high.

options.text: Please? I'll be very careful with it.

steps.player: Please? I'll be very careful with it.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: You know not what you deal with. There is evil in that mine and, whatever your assurances, I cannot risk you falling to the creatures within.

options.text: And you think you'll be safer in the mine than me?

steps.player: And you think you'll be safer in the mine than me?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Of course I'll be safe, my faith in Saradomin protects me.

options.text: I'll trade for it.

steps.player: I'll trade for it.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Saradomin provides for my every need. There is nothing you could offer me.

options.text: Pretty pretty please?

steps.player: Pretty pretty please?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Saradomin grant me patience. The answer is no.

options.text: I didn't want that key anyway.
I didn't want that key anyway.

steps.player: I didn't want that key anyway.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Witness the goodness of Saradomin, that he has granted you the wisdom to see our positions in perspective.

options.text: How does a lost artefact that was only legendary help?
Why was everyone in the mines slaughtered?
Can I borrow your key?
Where is the second entrance to the mines?
options.condition: After asking if there is another way into the mines:

options.text: How does a lost artefact that was only legendary help?

steps.player: How does a lost artefact that was only legendary help?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Although the amulet was lost, it is my hope that if I can make it into the mines I can craft another.

options.text: Why was everyone in the mines slaughtered?

steps.player: Why was everyone in the mines slaughtered? Surely it wasn't their fault that the crystals formed?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: It is said that some of the workers in the mines, merely from being in the presence of these crystals, found themselves bestowed with the love of Saradomin.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: The advantage to our cause was considered too great by some within Morytania. They set about mercilessly and brutally killing everyone in the mines rather than risk losing them to us.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Such is the treachery of the servants of evil, that they even destroy their own kind without a moments thought.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: The mines are now rumoured to be haunted by the souls of all those brutally and needlessly killed.

starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-after.speaker: Zealot
starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-after.text: Hello again. I'm afraid I'm rather preoccupied. What was it you wanted?

options.text: Can you explain the history of these mines again?
I've found the second entrance to the mine.
options.condition: Before reaching the sixth level of the mine:

steps.player: I've found the second entrance to the mine, I've managed to make it inside.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: You are foolhardy indeed should you venture inside. The presence of evil is strong within the mines. If you take the risk I shall pray for your safety, although I hold little hope for your safe return.
After turning the water valve and before going down the lift:

steps.player: Unfortunately I need a key to use the lift that goes to the lower levels.  Can you help?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Indeed? My own inquiries have led me into possession of a key. I was informed that this key would apparently afford entrance to the lower levels. It therefore seems likely that this is the key which you seek.

steps.player: Yes, that sounds like the one. May I borrow it?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I am afraid my task can be entrusted to nobody else. Saradomin has asked me alone to do this. I cannot take the slightest risk of losing this key. The stakes are too high.

options.text: Please? I'll be very careful with it.
I didn't want that key anyway.
I've made it in to the mines.
options.condition: After reaching the sixth level of the mine:

steps.player: I've made it in to the mines. Unfortunately some parts are too dark to navigate.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Ah ye of little faith. Let Saradomin guide you even in the darkest places. By his light you may reach your goal.

steps.player: As much as I respect your fanaticism, that was spectacularly unhelpful.

starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-after.player: G... g... g... ghost!  Scary ghost! Machinery flying everywhere.

starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-after.speaker: Zealot
starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-after.text: I warned you not to enter those mines. It sounds like you've met Dayth.  You must not go back down there.

options.text: Who did you say Dayth was again?

steps.player: Who did you say Dayth was again?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Treus Dayth was Zamorak's mage in charge of defending the ridge during the time of the orginal amulet.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Dayth failed and fell during an incursion by Saradominists, who then made it into the mines and were able to remove a shard of crystal.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Zamorak, furious at his mage, condemned Dayth's soul indefinitely to an existence of turmoil in the mines. Dayth's soul is bound to prevent the crystals from ever being reached again.

options.text: Nonsense, he'll be no match for me.

steps.player: Nonsense, he'll be no match for me.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I don't know if you think your persistance makes you heroic, but you must realise it's just going to get you killed.

starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-after.player: I met that Dayth character you talked about. He wasn't as tough as all that.

starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-after.speaker: Zealot
starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-after.text: I was afraid this would happen. The fear you must have experienced within those mines has left you delusional. There's no way you could have survived had you actually fought Dayth.

inside-the-mine-dropping-the-glowing-fun.text: When you drop the fungus it crumbles mysteriously to dust.

inside-the-mine-exiting-the-mine-via-the.text: As you crawl out into the sunlight, the strange fungus you are carrying crumbles to dust.

inside-the-mine-teleporting-out-with-the.text: The strange fungus you are carrying crumbles to dust.

inside-the-mine-pulling-track-levers.text: You pull the lever. The old points creak into place.

...plunging you straight into the middle of a flooded with water.
It's unlikely any of your light sources will dry off until you leave this dank cave.

steps.player: It's kind of dark down here. I should probably find a light source before going further.
Hey - my light source isn't working! I'd better find a more suitable one before trying to go any further.

You hear a disembodied voice laughing at you....Poor puny mortal. I'm going to have fun with you.
Treus appears, and strikes the player with the loading crane behind them.
I should deal with that ghost before trying to take the key again.

inside-the-mine-upon-killing-treus-dayth.text: As you make the killing strike, the machinery within the room falls silent.

You already have a key like that.
You should cut a shard from one of the crystals before leaving.
